Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the margin you want on wholesale, the days late before each reminder, the days before deliveries pause and the cost of waiting for money.

Write each cafe or shop on Accounts with its terms in days and its credit limit on Payment terms. The months together, the weekly value, the amount outstanding and the revenue of the last 12 months fill in.

Add each product an account takes every week on Standing orders (the same products delivered every week) with the weekdays, the price and the renewal date. The weekly value and a renewal flag fill in.
Write each weekly delivery on Wholesale deliveries and each product left over or sent back on Returns and unsold. The amount and the credit value fill in.

At month end write one row for each account on Invoices and its lines on Invoice lines. The amount outstanding, the days late and a timing flag fill in, and Monthly invoice builder checks the total and the due date.
Write each credit on Credit notes and keep the Wholesale price list up to date: the wholesale discount and the margin (the share of the price left after costs) fill in.
Record every late payer on Late payer log and every reminder on Payment reminders. Late reminder step tells you which reminder to send for the days late.
Use Client payments and Orders with balances for the money clients owe: the deposit (a part of the price paid to secure the date), the balance outstanding and the days overdue fill in.
Keep Account notes, Account reviews, Renewals and Prospects up to date: the follow-up flag, the price check and the days to the next review or the renewal fill in.
Use Cash due by week and Credit limit check before you accept a large order or plan your cash.
Use the 14 calculators before you send an invoice, a reminder or a renewal offer: invoice builder, late days, reminder step, credit note, account margin, credit limit, cash by week and more.

Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages). Read the Wholesale and Payments Dashboard and Charts every week.
Know which products earn and how much cash you can safely take
Profit, cash flow and growth for home bakeries and cake businesses
revenue from orders, wholesale and markets less ingredients, packaging, wages and overheads gives the profit and margin of each month
Profit by product and by order
each product and each order carries its share of overheads, so profit, margin and profit for each unit show what really earns
an order priced below its cost shows a loss flag before it is baked, with the price that breaks even
expected payments, invoices, costs and a planned big purchase give the weekly balance and flag every week under the cash floor
cash above the floor and profit after the tax set-aside give the most the owner can take without starving the business
Sales tax and business tax set-aside
every quarter shows the tax collected and the instalment to put away, with days to the due date and a flag
every review keeps its rating, topic and reply date, so the rating of each category and the unanswered reviews are clear
each client shows the days since the last order and a repeat flag, with ready messages for a thank you or a birthday cake
spend, enquiries and orders won give the cost for each order and the revenue for each 1 spent by source and campaign
Growth scenarios and new product payback
a second oven, a price rise or a new product shows the extra profit a month and the months to pay back the setup cost

One row for each month with the revenue streams and the costs you pay; the revenue, the profit after ingredients, packaging, wages and overheads and the margin fill in.
Product profit for the last 12 months
One row for each product with the units, revenue, cost and hours of the last 12 months; the overheads share, profit, margin and profit for each unit fill in, so a loss shows at once.
Order profit with the share of overheads
One row for each order with the price, the production cost and the labour hours; the overheads share, profit, margin and a flag fill in, so an order below its cost shows early.
Cash by month: in, out and closing balance
One row for each month with the opening cash, the money in and the money out; the net flow, the months of cover (closing cash over monthly running costs) and a floor flag fill in.
Cash forecast for the next 13 weeks
One row for each of the next 13 weeks with the payments, invoices, costs and any big purchase you plan; the net flow, closing balance and a floor flag fill in.
One row for each overhead you paid with the category, a short description and who you paid; the month fills in, so the charts group the money by category and month.
One row for each person and month with the hours, the rate and the amount; the share of the month wage bill fills in.
One row for each ingredient purchase with the category, the amount and the supplier; the month fills in, so ingredient costs can be followed by month.
Sales tax and business tax instalments
One row for each tax payment with the base, the rate, the amount and the due date (check your own local rules); the days to the due date and a flag fill in, so no payment is missed.
One row for each month with the money the owner took and the reason; the share of that month profit fills in, so a draw that is too large shows.
One row for each loan, lease or instalment plan with the monthly payment, the balance and the end date; the months left, the yearly cost and a flag fill in, so an ending payment is planned for.
Reviews with rating, topic and reply
One row for each review with the rating, the topic, the source and the day you replied; the days to reply and a flag fill in, so no review is left without an answer.
Repeat clients and the days since their last order
One row for each client with the orders, the spend and the first and last order; the days since the last order, the average order and a repeat flag fill in, so clients who went quiet are asked back.
Marketing spend and orders won by source
One row for each month and source with the spend, the enquiries, the orders won and their revenue; the cost for each order won and the return on spend fill in.
One row for each campaign with its dates, spend, orders and revenue; the days it ran, the cost for each order and the return on spend fill in, so you repeat what worked.
Growth scenarios: extra orders, price and cost
One row for each idea with the extra orders, the price change, the cost change and any fixed cost; the extra profit a month and a year and whether it beats your target fill in.
Product ideas with the yearly profit and payback
One row for each product idea with the expected price, cost, weekly units and setup cost; the margin, the yearly profit and the months to pay back the setup cost fill in.
One row for each month with the fixed costs (wages and overheads) and the share left after ingredients and packaging; break-even revenue and the margin of safety fill in.
Share left after food and packs
Budget for the year against the actual profit
One row for each month with the revenue and the cost you budgeted; the profit budget, the actual profit, the gap and a flag fill in from the Months sheet.

Type the price, the ingredient, packaging and energy costs and the labour minutes of one unit; see the labour and overheads share, the profit, the margin and the price for your wanted margin.

Type the spend, the orders won, the average order and your margin; see the revenue won, the profit it brought, the cost for each order and the orders you need to pay for the spend.

Owner: cash is below the floor in a week
Hello, the cash forecast shows {closing} in the week starting {week}, below the floor. Please check the big purchase and the invoices due.
Owner: the profit of the month
Hello, the profit for the month starting {month} is {profit} on revenue of {revenue}.
Hello, {product} made a profit of {profit} on revenue of {revenue} in the last 12 months. Please check its price and its cost.
Owner: check the safe owner draw
Hello, please check the safe owner draw for the month starting {month}. The draw was {amount}. Use the Safe owner draw calculator with the cash and the profit.
Owner: the tax set-aside is due
Hello, the tax payment of {amount} for the quarter starting {quarter_start} is due on {due_date}. Please keep the money set aside.
Owner: the month-end close is ready
Hello, the month-end close for the month starting {month} is ready: revenue {revenue}, profit {profit}.
Owner: a late invoice, cash is tight
Hello, the week starting {week} expects {expected_invoices} from invoices. If a late invoice does not arrive, the balance of {closing} may fall under the floor. Please call the account.
Owner: the yearly budget is ready
Hello, the budget for the month starting {month} is ready for review: revenue {revenue_budget}, cost {cost_budget}, profit {profit_budget}.
Hello, {product} earned a profit of {profit} on revenue of {revenue} in the last 12 months. Please keep its stock and its recipe in good order.
Owner: a growth scenario beats the plan
Hello, the scenario {scenario} adds {extra_profit} profit a month. Please review it.
Owner: a loan payment ends in 90 days
Hello, the payment for {item} ends on {end_date}, in about {months_left} months. Please plan what to do with the cash it frees.
Hello, wages for the month starting {month} were {wages} on revenue of {revenue}. Please check the hours.
Hello, the 13-week cash forecast is updated. The balance at the end of the week starting {week} is {closing}.
Owner: ingredient costs rose in a month
Hello, ingredient costs for the month starting {month} were {ingredients} on revenue of {revenue}. Please check the prices with the suppliers.
Hello, the profit and loss for the month starting {month} is attached: revenue {revenue}, profit {profit}.
Accountant: the cash report for a month
Hello, the cash report for the month starting {month} is attached: closing cash {closing}, net flow {net_flow}.
Hello, the tax set-aside for the quarter starting {quarter_start} is {amount}, due on {due_date}. Please confirm the amount.
Hello, please review the expense {expense_id} of {amount} for {description} in the month starting {month}.
Accountant: the year-end pack is ready
Hello, the year-end pack is ready. The last month in it starts on {month} with revenue {revenue} and profit {profit}.
Accountant: wages and sales for a month
Hello, wages and sales for the month starting {month}: wages {wages}, order revenue {order_revenue}, wholesale revenue {wholesale_revenue}.
Team: the wage budget for next quarter
Hello, the cost budget for the month starting {month} is {cost_budget}, wages included. Please tell me about extra hours before then.
Team: costs to watch in a product
Hello, please watch the costs of {product}: cost {cost} against revenue {revenue} in the last 12 months.
Hello, the cost budget for the month starting {month} is {cost_budget}. Please plan your bakes and your stock to match.
Client: thank you for your review
Hello {client}, thank you for your review of {product}. We are glad you chose us.
Client: we are sorry about your review
Hello {client}, we are sorry about your review of {product}. How can we put it right? Please reply to this message.
Client: thank you offer, repeat client
Hello {client}, thank you for ordering {orders} times. As a thank you we have an offer for your next order. Please reply to claim it.
Client: time for a birthday cake
Hello {client}, it is time to think about the next birthday cake. Your last order was on {last_order}. Shall we plan the next one?
Supplier: budget for next month orders
Hello, our cost budget for the month starting {month} is {cost_budget}. Please keep your prices steady and tell us about any change.

Open Start and type your company name and your own targets in the yellow cells: the profit margin you want, the cash floor, the usual owner draw, the tax set-aside share and the overheads for each production hour.
Fill Months once a month: orders, the three revenue streams and the costs. Revenue, profit and margin fill in, and Break-even rows and Budget read from them.
Check Product profit and Orders profit every month: the overheads share, the profit, the margin and a loss flag show which product or order earns and which loses money.
Write each month on Cash months and the next 13 weeks on Cash forecast. The closing balance and the floor flag fill in from the cash you have now, and a planned big purchase shows its effect.
Keep Expenses, Wages and Purchases up to date. The month fills in, so the charts group the money by category and month.
List every tax payment on Taxes (check your own local rules) and every draw on Owner draws. Days to due, flags and the share of the month profit fill in.
Write each loan, lease or instalment plan on Loans and equipment: the months left and a flag for a payment that ends in 90 days fill in.
Record every review on Reviews with the day you replied, and keep Repeat clients current: the days to reply, the repeat flag and the clients who have not ordered in 6 months fill in.
Write each month and each campaign on Marketing and Campaigns: the cost for each order won and the revenue for each 1 spent fill in.
Try ideas on Growth scenarios and Product pipeline: the extra profit a month and the months to pay back the setup cost fill in.
